learn: Which gases are greenhouse gases (CO2, methane, nitrous oxide, water vapour, ozone) and which are not (helium, nitric oxide)
SF6 is the most potent greenhouse gas
The ozone layer lies in the stratosphere and absorbs ultraviolet radiation
chapters.note: The "which is NOT a greenhouse gas" question repeats.

chapters.name: Environmental Laws and Conventions
learn: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
Ramsar Convention on wetlands: in force for India from 1982

chapters.name: Atmosphere and Weather
learn: Composition: nitrogen is about 78% of the air
Layers of the atmosphere and how temperature changes in each (thermosphere warms with height)
Rain: nimbostratus and cumulonimbus clouds; orographic rain falls on the windward side
Terms: dew point, eye of a cyclone, diurnal range of temperature, Van Allen belts

chapters.name: Solar System and Earth's Motions
learn: Order of the planets; Venus is the hottest; Pluto is a dwarf planet
Proxima Centauri is the nearest star to the Sun
Solstices and equinoxes: 21 June is the longest day in the Northern Hemisphere; the Sun is overhead at the Equator twice a year
Theories of origin: nebular hypothesis (Laplace), steady state theory (Fred Hoyle)
chapters.note: Repeats often, with very easy questions.

chapters.name: Rocks, Landforms and Weathering
learn: Weathering (breaking rocks in place) versus erosion (wearing away and carrying off)
Young fold mountains (Alps, Himalaya) versus old fold mountains (Aravalis, Urals, Appalachians)
Rock types with examples: sandstone is sedimentary
Most common elements of the Earth's crust; water vapour is the main volcanic gas

chapters.name: Soils and Soil Erosion
learn: Types of erosion: sheet erosion is the least visible; badlands form from gully erosion
Conservation methods: shelter belts, mulching
Humus is decayed organic matter in soil

chapters.name: Oceans, Tides and Coasts
learn: Spring and neap tides are about seven days apart
Salinity is grams of salt in 1000 g of seawater
Definitions: continental shelf, estuary, wavelength

chapters.name: Natural Hazards and Disasters
learn: Tsunami: a series of giant sea waves
Earthquake-prone regions of India
Landslide control: retaining walls, drainage, more vegetation

chapters.name: World Mountains and Deserts
learn: The Urals separate Asia from Europe
Deserts and their continent: Sahara (Africa), Atacama (South America, rich in copper)
Highest peaks of neighbouring countries: Pidurutalagala (Sri Lanka), Annapurna (Nepal)
Mount Everest was earlier called Peak XV

chapters.name: World Oceans, Rivers and Canals
learn: The Amazon is the largest river, in South America (Brazil)
Which ocean an island or sea belongs to: Madagascar in the Indian Ocean; the Black Sea is linked to the Atlantic
The Suez Canal is about 193 km long

chapters.name: Mauryan and Post-Mauryan Empires
learn: Chandragupta Maurya: overthrew the Nandas with Kautilya's help, fought Seleucus; Bindusara was his son
Ashoka: gave up war after Kalinga; inscriptions mostly in Brahmi; sites of the Minor Rock Edicts
Arthashastra by Kautilya and its administrative titles (Ashwadhyaksha, head of cavalry)
Junagadh inscription of the Shaka ruler Rudradaman
chapters.note: One of the three most asked ancient-history chapters.

chapters.name: Vedic Age
learn: Vedic names of rivers: Vitasta (Jhelum), Askini (Chenab), Parushni (Ravi), Vipash (Beas)
Indra is the leading god of the Rig Veda
Vedic texts by number: six Vedangas, 20 kandas of the Atharvaveda
Society: gotra, the four purusharthas, duties of the varnas
chapters.note: Repeats often.

chapters.name: Ancient Literature, Science and Education
learn: Books and authors: Arthashastra (Kautilya), Ashtadhyayi (Panini), Mricchakatika (Sudraka)
Scientists: Aryabhata (astronomy), Varahamihira, Charaka (medicine), Sushruta (surgery)
Universities: Takshashila, Nalanda (Bihar), Vikramshila (founded by Dharmapala)
The Vikrama Era began in 57 BC
chapters.note: Asked steadily, almost always as a book-author or scholar-field match.

chapters.name: Gupta and Post-Gupta Period
learn: Allahabad Pillar inscription records Samudragupta's conquests; the Mehrauli Iron Pillar does not rust
Harshavardhana: Pushyabhuti dynasty of Thaneswar, defeated by Pulakesin II on the Narmada
Hiuen Tsang visited in Harsha's time and wrote Si-yu-ki
Kannauj replaced Pataliputra as the centre of north India (Maukharis)
Founders of smaller kingdoms, e.g. Mayurasharman of the Kadambas

chapters.name: Prehistory and Indus Valley
learn: Location of sites: Mehrgarh near the Bolan Pass; Harappan sites in Gujarat, Rajasthan and Haryana
Chalcolithic cultures and their region (Jorwe culture in Maharashtra)
Stone Age tools, e.g. the celt is a Neolithic tool

chapters.name: South Indian Kingdoms and Sangam Age
learn: Sangam literature came from assemblies of poets at Madurai
Arikamedu was a port trading with Rome
Pallava rulers such as Mahendravarman I

chapters.name: Buddhism and Jainism
learn: Buddha was born at Lumbini
The Tripitakas are the Buddhist sacred books

chapters.name: Mahajanapadas and Magadha
learn: Capitals of the Mahajanapadas (Champa was the capital of Anga)
Magadha dynasties and their kings (Ajatashatru of the Haryanka dynasty)

chapters.name: Mughal Empire
learn: Babur and the Battle of Khanwa (1527) against Rana Sanga and his allies
Humayun regained Delhi in 1555; Sher Shah's administration was the model for Akbar
Akbar: Bairam Khan, Todar Mal's zabti revenue system, Ain-i-Akbari, tomb at Sikandra
Jahangir: earlier Prince Salim, wife Nur Jahan, Sir Thomas Roe at his court
Aurangzeb died in 1707; court chronicles were written in Persian
chapters.note: The most asked history chapter; the Battle of Khanwa came up three times.

chapters.name: Turkish Invasions and Delhi Sultanate
learn: Order of dynasties: Slave, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid (founded by Khizr Khan), Lodi
Muhammad bin Tughlaq's token currency: copper coins in place of the silver tanka
Iltutmish's group of forty nobles (Chahalgani); Balban and the Bengal revolt
Alauddin Khalji's taxes; departments such as Diwan-i-Insha
Invasions: Mahmud of Ghazni at Somnath (1026), Battles of Tarain (1191), Timur (1398)
chapters.note: Repeats often; the Tughlaqs are asked most.

chapters.name: Early Medieval Kingdoms and Cholas
learn: Dynasty, founder and capital: Rashtrakutas (Dantidurga, Malkhed), Pratiharas (Kannauj), Pallavas (Kanchi), Senas (Lakhnauti)
Chola village assemblies: Sabha for Brahmana villages, Ur for ordinary villages; shalabhoga land for schools
Palas: Dharmapala founded Vikramashila and supported Nalanda
Terms: samanta, nagara-shreshthi

chapters.name: Vijayanagara and Regional Kingdoms
learn: Vijayanagara: founded by the Sangama dynasty; capital Hampi in Karnataka
Regional dynasties: Ahoms (Assam), Wadiyars (Mysore), small kingdoms of Kerala

chapters.name: Medieval Literature and Travellers
learn: Chand Bardai wrote Prithviraj Raso
Al-Biruni wrote Kitab-ul-Hind

chapters.name: Sikh Gurus
learn: Guru Arjan Dev, the fifth Guru, built the Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) at Amritsar

chapters.name: Gandhian Mass Movements
learn: Years of the main events in order: Champaran 1917, Kheda 1918, Jallianwala Bagh 1919, Chauri Chaura 1922, Bardoli 1928, Dandi March 1930, Quit India 1942
Non-Cooperation was called off after Chauri Chaura
Quit India: Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank; Kushal Konwar was hanged
Peasant movements: Patel led Bardoli; Sahajanand Saraswati formed the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha (1929)
Jallianwala Bagh and General Dyer's "crawling order"
chapters.note: Chronology (arrange the events in order) is a favourite format.

chapters.name: Revolutionary Movement
learn: Kakori train robbery, 1925: Ram Prasad Bismil and Ashfaqulla Khan of the HRA (founded 1924)
Abroad: India House in London (Shyamji Krishna Varma, 1905); Ghadar Party in San Francisco (1913)
Khudiram Bose was hanged at Muzaffarpur in 1908
Chittagong Armoury Raid and its members
chapters.note: Repeats often; Kakori alone was asked three times.

chapters.name: Congress and Political Organisations
learn: Indian National Congress was founded in 1885
Indian Association, 1876, Calcutta: Surendranath Banerjee and Anand Mohan Bose
Sessions: Belgaum 1924 (the only one Gandhi presided over), Karachi 1931 (Fundamental Rights resolution)
Congress Socialist Party was founded in 1934

chapters.name: Round Table Conferences and Poona Pact
learn: Second Round Table Conference, London 1931: Gandhi was the only Congress representative
Third Round Table Conference was held in 1932
Poona Pact, 1932: between Gandhi and Ambedkar
C R Formula (1944) was proposed by C. Rajagopalachari
chapters.note: The Second Round Table Conference (1931, Gandhi as sole Congress delegate) was asked three times.

chapters.name: Freedom Fighters and Titles
learn: Popular titles: Deshbandhu (Chittaranjan Das), Andhra Kesari (T. Prakasam), Gandhi Buri (Matangini Hazra)

chapters.name: Subhas Chandra Bose and INA
learn: Provisional Government of Free India was proclaimed in Singapore on 21 October 1943
Bose formed the Free India Legion in Germany
Slogan: "Give me blood and I will give you freedom"

chapters.name: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi
learn: Bengal was partitioned in 1905 by Lord Curzon
The Muslim League supported the partition

chapters.name: Socio-Religious Reform Movements
learn: Raja Ram Mohan Roy: Atmiya Sabha (1814), Brahmo Samaj (1828)
Founder and organisation: Arya Samaj (Dayanand Saraswati), Prarthana Samaj (Atmaram Pandurang, 1867), Aligarh Movement (Sir Syed Ahmad Khan), Theosophical Society (Annie Besant)
Ramakrishna Mission and Belur Math (Vivekananda)
Reformers of Maharashtra: Jyotiba and Savitribai Phule
Parsi reform: Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha (Dadabhai Naoroji)
chapters.note: Repeats often. Learn founder, organisation and year together.

chapters.name: Governors-General and British Policies
learn: Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal
Lord Ripon repealed the Vernacular Press Act; the Ilbert Bill controversy
Age of Consent Act, 1891
Viceroy at the time of an event (e.g. Bengal famine of 1943)

chapters.name: British Conquest and Battles
learn: Battle of Plassey, 1757: East India Company against Siraj-ud-Daulah
Third Battle of Panipat, 1761; Battle of Saragarhi, 1897
Awadh was annexed in 1856 (last Nawab Wajid Ali Shah)
Lahore was the capital of Maharaja Ranjit Singh

chapters.name: Advent of Europeans
learn: The Portuguese came first; the English East India Company was chartered in 1600
First settlements: English factory at Hugli (1651), French at Chandannagar (1673)

chapters.name: Post-Independence India
learn: Liberation of Goa from the Portuguese, 1961
1971 war: Sam Manekshaw was Army Chief
Lahore Declaration, 1999 (Vajpayee's bus journey)
Foreign leaders' first visits and other landmark events after 1947

chapters.name: Land Revenue and Economic Impact
learn: Permanent Settlement: Cornwallis, 1793
Ryotwari system and the theory of rent behind it
Dadabhai Naoroji wrote Poverty and Un-British Rule in India

chapters.name: Revolt of 1857
learn: Began at Meerut on 10 May 1857
Leaders and centres: Mangal Pandey, Kunwar Singh, Begum Hazrat Mahal, Rani Lakshmibai (samadhi in Gwalior)

chapters.name: Monuments and Heritage Sites
learn: Who built what and where: Charminar (Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, Hyderabad), Konark Sun Temple (Narasimhadeva I)
Buddhist sites: Sanchi stupa, Ghoom Monastery (Darjeeling)
Caves: Elephanta (Maharashtra), Lomas Rishi in the Barabar Hills (Bihar)
Modern and colonial buildings: Victoria Terminus, Open Hand Monument by Le Corbusier
Mathura school of sculpture in the Kushana period
chapters.note: Asked in about one paper in five.

chapters.name: Mughal and Indo-Islamic Architecture
learn: Builder of each monument: Taj Mahal (Shah Jahan), Agra Fort (Akbar), Bibi Ka Maqbara (Azam Shah)
Akbar's tomb is at Sikandra; Panch Mahal is at Fatehpur Sikri
Gol Gumbaz at Bijapur has the largest dome in India

chapters.name: Philosophy and Cultural Institutions
learn: Founders of schools of philosophy: Kanada (Vaisheshika), Charvaka (Lokayata)
Shantiniketan: founded by Rabindranath Tagore in 1901; Kala Bhavana is its art school

chapters.name: World History
learn: French Revolution gave the ideals of liberty, equality and fraternity
World War I began in 1914
Mesopotamians wrote in cuneiform on clay tablets
chapters.note: Rarely asked in SSC.

chapters.name: Constitutional Amendments
learn: Article 368 gives the amendment procedure
Key amendments: 1st (1951), 7th (states reorganisation), 26th (privy purses), 42nd (socialist, secular, integrity), 44th (property), 61st (voting age 18)
Less common ones asked: 40th, 60th (profession tax), 88th (service tax)
chapters.note: A must-do list: amendment number matched to what it changed.

chapters.name: Making of the Constitution
learn: Constituent Assembly committees and their chairmen; the Drafting Committee had seven members
Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution; the National Anthem was adopted on 24 January 1950
Borrowed features: Directive Principles (Ireland), Fundamental Duties (USSR), independent judiciary (USA)
chapters.note: Repeats often. One 2022 shift asked several detailed Constituent Assembly questions.

chapters.name: Preamble, Parts and Schedules
learn: Words of the Preamble: which are present (sovereign, justice, liberty, fraternity) and which are not (federal)
Twelve Schedules and what each covers: Second (salaries), Eighth (languages)
Subjects in the Union, State and Concurrent Lists
Which Part covers what: Part V (Articles 52 to 78) is the Union Executive

chapters.name: Union, States and Citizenship
learn: Article 1: India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States
Citizenship: Articles 5 to 11 (Part II); Citizenship Act, 1955
Official language: Article 343 (Hindi in Devanagari), Article 347
Special provisions: Article 371F for Sikkim
Earlier names of states (Arunachal Pradesh was NEFA)

chapters.name: Forms of Government
learn: Three organs: legislature, executive, judiciary
Presidential versus parliamentary system
The United Kingdom has no written constitution
Pressure groups try to influence policy; they do not contest elections

chapters.name: Emergency Provisions
learn: The President proclaims an emergency
Parliament must approve a national emergency within one month

chapters.name: Parliament
learn: Parliament is the President plus both Houses (Article 79); quorum is one-tenth (Article 100)
Rajya Sabha: six-year term, seats by state under the Fourth Schedule (Article 80)
Money Bills: the Rajya Sabha can only recommend changes; a bill becomes an Act with the President's assent
Speaker decides disqualification under the Tenth Schedule
Public Accounts Committee examines CAG reports
No-confidence motion; vote on account; sessions of Parliament
chapters.note: The most asked polity chapter, in more than one paper in four.

chapters.name: President and Vice-President
learn: Articles: 53 (executive power), 59 (conditions of office), 61 (impeachment)
Vice-President: minimum age 35; S. Radhakrishnan was the first
Background of past Presidents

chapters.name: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
learn: Order and tenures of Prime Ministers: Charan Singh followed Morarji Desai; shortest tenures (Gulzarilal Nanda, Chandra Shekhar)
No limit on the number of terms a Prime Minister can serve

chapters.name: Flagship Government Schemes
learn: Launch year of each scheme: Swachh Bharat (2 October 2014), Digital India (2015), Fit India (2019), NIPUN Bharat (2021)
Aim of each: Jal Jeevan Mission, Stand-Up India, PM-ABHIM, Swajal
Swachh Survekshan is run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
National Urban Sanitation Policy colour codes for cities
chapters.note: Sanitation and drinking-water schemes were asked heavily in 2022 papers.

chapters.name: Important Acts and Laws
learn: Years of key Acts: Hindu Marriage Act (1955), Hindu Succession Act (1956), Domestic Violence Act (2005), Right to Education Act (2009)
RTI (Amendment) Act, 2019: the Centre fixes the term of information commissioners

chapters.name: Fundamental Rights
learn: Article numbers: 14 to 18 (equality), 19 (freedoms), 20, 21 (life and liberty), 22 (arrest), 24 (child labour)
Right to Property was removed by the 44th Amendment
Recent Supreme Court readings, e.g. internet access under Article 19
chapters.note: Asked as "which Article deals with...". Learn Articles 12 to 35 by number.

chapters.name: Fundamental Duties and Directive Principles
learn: Article 51A: the list of duties, including scientific temper, protecting public property, and educating children aged 6 to 14
Article 39A: equal justice and free legal aid
chapters.note: Fundamental Duties are asked in recent papers; know the full list.

chapters.name: Panchayati Raj and Local Bodies
learn: 73rd Amendment (Panchayats, Part IX) and 74th Amendment (municipalities)
Articles: 243E (five-year term), 243-I (State Finance Commission), 243K (State Election Commissioner)
Gram Sabha is the base of the system
Reservation for women in local bodies

chapters.name: Governor and State Legislature
learn: Governor takes the oath before the Chief Justice of the High Court
One Governor can serve two or more states (7th Amendment)
A Money Bill in a state assembly needs the Governor's recommendation

chapters.name: Constitutional Bodies
learn: Articles: 148 (CAG), 324 (Election Commission)
CAG: what it audits, and that it heads the Indian Audit and Accounts Department
Election Commission became a multi-member body in 1989
State PSC chairman: appointed by the Governor, removed only by the President
Chairman of the latest Finance Commission
chapters.note: Asked in about one paper in eight.

chapters.name: Judiciary and Writs
learn: The five writs and their use: quo warranto (right to hold office), prohibition (stops a lower court)
Writ powers: Article 32 (Supreme Court), Article 226 (High Courts)
Supreme Court decisions bind all courts
Removal of judges: Justice V. Ramaswami faced the first impeachment motion
Malimath Committee on criminal justice reform

chapters.name: Reserve Bank and Monetary Policy
learn: Repo rate and reverse repo rate: who borrows from whom, and that the RBI fixes both
RBI raises the repo rate to control inflation
CRR: cash reserves banks must keep with the RBI
Inflation targeting got legal backing through the 2016 amendment to the RBI Act, 1934
RBI facts: C. D. Deshmukh was the first Indian Governor; banknotes show the value in 15 languages on the back
chapters.note: Repo and reverse repo definitions repeat often.

chapters.name: Banks in India
learn: Regional Rural Banks: ownership is Centre 50%, sponsor bank 35%, state 15%; set up on the Narasimham committee's advice
Bank mergers: Dena Bank and Vijaya Bank into Bank of Baroda (2019)
Domestic Systemically Important Banks: SBI, ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank
SBI was created by its own Act, not by nationalisation

chapters.name: Rural Credit and Self-Help Groups
learn: Institutional credit (banks, cooperatives, RRBs) versus non-institutional credit (moneylenders, traders)
Self-help groups: members decide savings and loans themselves
NABARD started the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme in 1992-93
MFIN is the self-regulatory body of microfinance institutions
chapters.note: Asked from 2022 onwards, based on NCERT class 10 economics.

chapters.name: Financial Markets and Payments
learn: Bombay Stock Exchange was founded in 1875 by Premchand Roychand
Regulators: the Forward Markets Commission regulated commodity futures (now merged with SEBI)
Payment terms: merchant discount rate, the 22-character UTR number in RTGS
Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019

chapters.name: Demand, Supply and Types of Goods
learn: Normal, inferior and Giffen goods: how demand moves with income and price
Public goods are non-rival and non-excludable; private goods are rival and excludable
Derived demand: demand for a factor of production comes from demand for the final good
Movement along a curve (expansion or contraction) versus a shift of the curve; equilibrium price
Price elasticity = % change in quantity ÷ % change in price
chapters.note: Among the most repeated economics chapters; inferior and normal goods come up again and again.

chapters.name: Economic Terms and Thinkers
learn: Barter: goods themselves act as the medium of exchange
Marginal propensity to consume lies between 0 and 1
Terms: Golden Handshake (voluntary retirement scheme), trickle-down theory, income as a flow
Economists: Keynes (England, Keynesian economics), Haberler (opportunity cost theory of trade)

chapters.name: Inflation
learn: Inflation is a sustained rise in the general price level
Core inflation leaves out food and energy prices
Real interest rate = nominal interest rate − inflation rate

chapters.name: Markets and Production
learn: Monopoly: a market with a single seller
An isoquant is another way of showing the production function
chapters.note: Asked only in older papers (2017).

chapters.name: Government Budget and Fiscal Policy
learn: Revenue versus capital items: salaries are revenue expenditure, disinvestment proceeds are a capital receipt
Deficit budget and deficit financing: spending more than revenue
FRBM target: fiscal deficit of 3% of GDP
Vote on account (only expenditure) versus interim budget (full statement)
Proportional income tax works as an automatic stabiliser

chapters.name: Taxation and GST
learn: Direct versus indirect taxes; GST is an indirect tax
Progressive, proportional and regressive taxes
GST facts: France was the first country to adopt it; GST Council rate decisions
Order in which taxes came to India: land revenue, sales tax, MODVAT (1986), service tax (1994)

chapters.name: Five Year Plans and NITI Aayog
learn: Planning Commission set up in 1950 (Nehru as chairman); replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015, chaired by the Prime Minister
Focus and facts of individual plans: First Plan growth 3.6%, Fifth Plan Garibi Hatao, Eighth Plan (1992-97) and economic reforms
Plan Holiday: three annual plans, 1966 to 1969
National Development Council includes all Chief Ministers
NITI Aayog prepares the SDG India Index
chapters.note: Repeats often.

chapters.name: Inequality, Unemployment and SDGs
learn: Lorenz curve shows income distribution
Disguised unemployment is a form of underemployment
SDG 6 is clean water and sanitation

chapters.name: Agriculture and Green Revolution
learn: Green Revolution: began in the 1960s with wheat, Punjab gained most, it over-used natural resources
Difference between the first and the second Green Revolution
Farm schemes: PM-AASHA has three parts (PSS, PDPS, PPSS); PM Fasal Bima premium is at most 2% for kharif crops
Marketable surplus and commercialisation of agriculture
chapters.note: Asked more in recent papers.

chapters.name: Industries and Industrial Policy
learn: Base year of the Index of Industrial Production (2011-12)
TISCO was set up in 1907 by Dorabji Tata
Which companies are public sector undertakings (e.g. BHEL)
Main changes made by the industrial policies (1980 raised limits for tiny units)

chapters.name: National Income
learn: Three methods of measuring national income: product, income and expenditure
GDP deflator = nominal GDP ÷ real GDP (also called the implicit price deflator)
Depreciation is consumption of fixed capital
GDP at market prices versus factor cost (taxes and subsidies); how personal income is derived from national income
Definition of GDP and what its sector-wise split shows
chapters.note: Definitions and formulas repeat; the three measurement methods were asked more than once.

chapters.name: Exchange Rate and Balance of Payments
learn: Devaluation lowers a currency's value: exports get cheaper, imports costlier
Real exchange rate and the Purchasing Power Parity theory
Balance of Payments records all transactions with the rest of the world

chapters.name: International Trade and Organisations
learn: Dumping: selling abroad below cost
Heckscher-Ohlin model: countries export goods that use their abundant factors
The IMF publishes the World Economic Outlook
